messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — GPU capacity exhaustion in us-west-2 (cluster: inference-prod). Autoscaler reports repeated failures to create/attach GPU nodegroup. Queue length for inference-requests has spiked x6. Paging on-call: @sre_oncall :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Pager triggered (P1) — multiple 504s observed for /v1/generate. Rule: gpu-queue-throttle. See metrics dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/c/ai-inference

sre_oncall: I'm on it. Looking at cluster-autoscaler logs now. Can someone add context on recent changes? @eng-runtime or @infra?

devon: No infra deploys in last 2 hrs. We did push a runtime model rollout earlier but that shouldn't touch nodegroup configs. I can tail the autoscaler logs:
```
I0315 10:02:12.345678 autoscaler.go:123] Failed to increase desired capacity: instance profile mismatch: launch template id lt-0abc123 does not match attach policy arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/InferenceNodeRole
```

maya: Logs show ASG attach policy drift — looks like the nodegroup's launch template was accidentally rotated in a recent infra change and the instance profile role was swapped to `InferenceNodeRole-v2` which doesn't have ec2:AttachNetworkInterface. That causes the attach to fail and CA to bail.

lucas: Also seeing taint mismatch on the new node template: it has `node.kred=dedicated:NoSchedule` but scheduler expects `kred/gpu=exclusive`. Pods are unschedulable even if nodes are created. So two blockers: IAM/attach perms + unexpected taint key/value.

sre_oncall: Good catch. Immediate mitigation plan: 1) stop autoscaler from retrying to create broken nodegroup (so it doesn't thrash), 2) create a temporary nodegroup with known-good launch template/instance profile, 3) patch taints or create a toleration on the critical pods to allow scheduling until we roll the nodegroups properly.

infra: I can spin up a temporary nodegroup using the stable launch template `lt-stable-2025-11-01` and attach instance profile `InferenceNodeRole-stable`. Spawning now, will bump ASG desired by +6 GPUs (estimated).

devon: While infra does that, I'll flip the autoscaler to maintenance mode: set `--scale-down-enabled=false` and pause reconciliation for the ASG so it stops deleting the failing launchconfig attempts. Command: `kubectl -n kube-system annotate deployment cluster-autoscaler autoscaler.k8s.io/paused=true` (we'll revert later).

eng-runtime: For short term routing, we can enable fallback model variant on the ingress gateway to route 20% of requests to cpu-backed nodes to reduce pressure. Not ideal, but it will reduce queue growth for critical customers. Rolling policy: `nginx-route:weight=cpu-fallback:20`.

sre_oncall: infra — update?

infra: Temporary nodegroup launched. Instances provisioning (ASG desired=+6). Instances are `i-0f1ab2c3`. Boot logs show they assume `InferenceNodeRole-stable`. Kube join succeeded: `kubectl get nodes` shows 4/6 in Ready state so far.

lucas: I'm removing the unexpected taint from the new nodes so pods can land: `kubectl taint nodes -l launchtemplate=lt-stable-2025-11-01 node.kred=dedicated:NoSchedule-` — doing that now. Pods are scheduling.

sre_oncall: Traffic and queue metrics improving — queue depth down 60% in 12m, error rate for /v1/generate down from 18% to 3%. Still watching for any ASG flapping.

maya: For root cause we need to track how launch template drift happened. Preliminary find: an automated infra rollout yesterday modified launch template tags; an internal tool selected `InferenceNodeRole-v2` by mistake due to a tag mismatch. It lacked `ec2:AttachNetworkInterface` and didn't set expected taint key.

infra: Filing immediate infra ticket to revert LT tags and add validation in the CI job that rotates launch templates. Ticket: INFRA-4722. I'll also run an IAM policy diff and re-add `ec2:AttachNetworkInterface` to the v2 role as an extra resilience measure.

sre_oncall: Customer impact check — Maya, can you estimate percent of customers affected and notable cohorts?

maya: From request logs: ~32% of generation requests in the last 20m were queued > 2s and 18% returned 504s before mitigation. Impact concentrated on standard and high-concurrency clients (tenants T41, T58). Free-tier saw degraded latency but few errors. We should notify CS for T41 and T58.

devon: I'll open a concise customer-facing incident note for CS: short summary + ETA for full remediation.

ops-bot: NOTE: autoscaler reconciliation paused by devon at 10:18 UTC.

sre_oncall: Next steps and owners:
- infra: INFRA-4722 (revert LT tags + CI validation) — owner @infra
- eng-runtime: add tolerant toleration for critical pods to prevent future taint mismatches (short-term) — owner @eng-runtime
- devex: update runbook with `pause-autoscaler` and temporary-nodegroup steps — owner @devon
- maya: craft customer impact summary and notify CS for T41/T58 — owner @maya

lucas: I'll follow up to remove the temporary nodes once the launch templates are reconciled. Plan: cordon + drain temporary nodes, then reduce ASG desired back to pre-incident levels.

sre_oncall: Timeline: incident declared 10:02 UTC, mitigation (temp nodegroup + taint fix) reduced user-visible errors by 10:30 UTC. I'm leaving this as P1 until LT tags are reverted and CA can auto-scale normally.

devon: Drafted CS message and posted to #customer-notices for review.

infra: Reverted tags on `lt-0abc123` and updated role policy. Kicking a small nodegroup rollout to ensure CA can create nodes with the corrected LT.

sre_oncall: Re-enabling autoscaler reconciliation now (`autoscaler.k8s.io/paused=false`). Watching for new CA events.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged as ongoing — next paging if error rate > 5% for 5m.

sre_oncall: Autoscaler successfully created/attached a nodegroup using corrected LT at 11:02 UTC. New nodes joined Ready and pods drained from temp nodes. Lowering priority: we will keep P1 open until postmortem and CI checks.

eng-runtime: Post-incident action items: add a validation step in the launch-template rotation job to assert taint keys and instance-profile permissions (automation test). Also add an alert for any CA `Failed to increase desired capacity` messages that include `instance profile` to trigger infra runbook earlier.

maya: Sending targeted notices to T41/T58 support reps now.

sre_oncall: Thanks everyone. I'll start the incident write-up and assign postmortem owners. Please add any logs/commands you ran to the ticket.

ops-bot: Incident auto-summary (created): "GPU autoscaling blocked by launch-template/instance-profile drift + unexpected taints — temp nodegroup mitigated impact; root cause infra LT rotation bug; actions: revert LT tags, CI validation, alerting rules". Link: https://incidents.internal/1779991111

devon: Adding runbook improvement PR: https://github.com/redwood/runbooks/pull/211

lucas: Final state: queue normalized, error rate <1% for 15m, decommissioning temporary nodegroup in 10m.

sre_oncall: Closing the live mitigation channel. Postmortem owners: @maya (customer impact), @infra (infra root cause), @eng-runtime (automation/tests)."
